lead_headline: Foreclosure filings surge 40% week-over-week to 42 cases—highest weekly volume since February—as single $57M Arapahoe outlier dominates $71M total exposure

restaurant.blurb: 7 new leads today climb active count to 65 (32 openings, 33 closures)—first closure majority since tracker launch. Opening side: Jersey Mike's expands Quebec Square (Stapleton), Chaton Bakery preps Parker Road debut near H Mart (Kennedy), FiNO Mediterranean launches inside renovated All Inn Hotel (City Park). Closure surge: Reunion Bakery exits The Source (relocating to Pearl Street after 7 years), Bar Amorina shutters Clayton Hotel (10-month run, Cherry Creek), Smashburger closes Lowry Town Center (May 2025, 3-year tenure). Geographic shift: Union Station's opening dominance fades—today's leads scatter across Stapleton, Kennedy, Cherry Creek periphery. Yesterday's triple-header (Paperboy, Black Rock, The Barn) marks week's peak opening cluster; closure backlog now fills from delayed detections vs fresh shutdowns.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 filings this week—up 40% from prior week's 30—sustain March's volatility as $57M Arapahoe outlier (2038 S Vaughn commercial case) inflates $71M aggregate exposure; next-largest filing drops to $795K Weld County property.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend March's unprecedented drought—fourth consecutive week without filings. Monthly count remains flatlined at zero through 25 days, marking longest silence since tracker inception. No pending applications visible across Denver, Arapahoe, Boulder, Jefferson counties. Historical context: January-February averaged 12 weekly applications; March's collapse suggests seasonal lull or systemic reporting delay. Watch April 1 for quarterly application surge as operators target summer patio season.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today (Instagram Box Box Colfax dining room post) holds 7-day total at 51—up 21% from prior week's 42, fourth straight week above 40-mention floor. Denver Post dominates with 21 pickups (41% share), Instagram delivers 10, Hoodline and Facebook tie at 5 each. Notable coverage: Wilderness Exchange closure (Post), Zeppelin Station loan settlement (Business Journals dual-pickup), THC drink federal concern (CED Clinic). Source concentration tightens: Post plus social platforms command 75% of volume—Post dependency intensifies vs prior week's 46% share.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 today (1 new, 0 canceled) nudges MTD to +44 (+1.8/day), 90-day cumulative to +112 (+1.2/day). Today's modest gain follows yesterday's +4 surge—seven-day window tallies +17 net (27 new, 10 canceled), matching prior week's +17 exactly but with higher churn (10 vs 6 cancels). Recent pattern: acquisition decelerates to 3.9/day vs early-March's 4.5+ peaks, cancellation creeps to 1.4/day from mid-month's 0.8 floor—retention slippage offsets steady new-subscriber flow. March tracking toward 48-52 net monthly gain if pace holds, still 25% above February baseline but losing steam vs explosive early-month momentum.
